title: R' Yosi ben Petros
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman states that he was R' Yehoshua ben Levi’s father-in-law, as explicitly stated in Moed Katan ch. 3, halakhah 4, 13b; and there: “R-Y-B-P, the former father-in-law of R-Y-B-L” (Korban HaEdah explains that R' Yehoshua ben Levi had two wives and this was his first father-in-law; but Seder HaDorot copied the Yerushalmi in the wording “R' Yosi bar Petrom, father-in-law of R-Y-B-L, had an incident [of mourning] before them; Bar Kappara sent him two disciples to study with him,” etc. From his words, Hyman infers that this was his reading in the Yerushalmi, and not that he had two wives).
And in Bereshit Rabbah 94:5: B-Q and R' Yosef (Hyman says: should read Yosi) bar Petros—one said, “How Father was eager,” etc.

Hyman cites Vayikra Rabbah ch. 12: Zevadi bar Levi and R' Yose ben Partam (Hyman says: should read Petros) and the Rabbis—one said, etc. So too it is in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, 158. And in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah ch. 3, halakhah 1, and Tanchuma Miketz9: Zevadi bar Levi and R' Yose bar Piters and R-Y-B-L said three verses at his death: “For this every pious one will pray,” etc. And in Midrash Tehillim chapter 5, with the terminal locator ד׳ retained, Hyman says its R' Yose bar Pinchas reading is an error.

notes.text: Korban HaEdah’s first-father-in-law explanation and Seder HaDorot’s differently placed קדמייהו are competing reported readings; no second Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi is created. The final Midrash Tehillim locator is chapter5 with the terminal ד׳ still needing confirmation.

Those two English locators follow the print without changing the Hebrew. The whole consulted modern Jerusalem Talmud passage is 3:5, paragraph 20: it names Yose bar Petrus, calls him Yehoshua ben Levi’s first father-in-law, and has Bar Kappara send two students to study with him. This does not independently establish two marriages or collate Seder HaDorot’s differently placed קדמייהו. The whole Bereshit Rabbah 94:5 directly names Bar Kappara and Yosef bar Patros with “one said, how Father was eager”; Hyman’s correction to Yosi remains his definite editorial judgment. The consulted Vayikra Rabbah 7:2 has Zavdi ben Levi and Yosei ben Petras, while Hyman’s print gives chapter 12 and Partam.
